tldr: This is a theme thread, not one event: three separate items treat vLLM as the default open serving stack. It opened with Warmctl, a Show HN tool for faster vLLM cold starts, then vLLM shipped day-0 support for Baidu's ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview through a plugin.
whats_new: Humanity's Last System (HLS), an open benchmark, gives coding agents live GPU sandboxes for up to 36 hours to build inference servers, then verifies them and scores their speed against vLLM-style baselines.
why_it_matters: vLLM is now the reference point for serving: new models ship as vLLM plugins, tools patch its cold starts, and agent benchmarks measure themselves against it.

beats.headline: Warmctl targets vLLM cold-start latency
beats.summary: A Show HN tool aimed at the slow startup of vLLM servers.

beats.headline: Day-0 vLLM support for ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview via plugin
beats.summary: A 280B-parameter MoE with 14B active per token runs through the vllm-ERNIE plugin on vllm==0.32.0.

beats.headline: HLS benchmark asks agents to build inference engines that beat vLLM
beats.summary: Agent-built servers are verified and scored for speed against vLLM-style baselines.

open_questions: Does any agent-built server in HLS beat the vLLM baseline on verified speed, and on which models?
Does ERNIE 5.5 Flash support move from the vllm-ERNIE plugin into mainline vLLM?
Does Warmctl publish cold-start measurements against a stock vLLM startup?
take_for_builders: For ERNIE 5.5 Flash, pin vllm==0.32.0 with the vllm-ERNIE plugin. Treat HLS results as research until verified scores beat your own vLLM baseline on your models.

day_captions.0a0ce400ec58ec0b: Shows a model lab shipping launch-day serving support as a vLLM plugin pinned to a specific vLLM release.
day_captions.781ec9697da4f86b: Turns vLLM into the benchmark target for agent-written inference engines.
